[USER] The user requested an explanation of how to use research goals and objectives to identify the target user group and develop interview questions.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Research goals and objectives can help identify the target user group and develop interview questions that are specifically designed to elicit the insights needed to achieve those goals and objectives.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Identifying the target user group is a crucial step in conducting effective user interviews.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The research goals and objectives should guide the selection of participants who fit the desired demographic profile or have relevant experience with the product or service being tested.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] An example target user group for a mobile app research goal could be smartphone users between the ages of 18-35 who frequently use apps for social networking, messaging, and productivity.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Interview questions should be designed to uncover the behaviors, attitudes, motivations, and pain points of the target user group.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Interview questions should be open-ended and non-leading, allowing participants to provide detailed and honest feedback.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Questions should be organized in a logical and coherent manner, flowing from more general to more specific topics.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The interview may begin with broad questions about the participant's experience with mobile apps, followed by more specific questions about their use of social networking apps and productivity apps.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] The interview may conclude with questions about their overall impressions of the new mobile app being tested.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] Using research goals and objectives to identify the target user group and develop interview questions is essential for conducting effective user interviews that generate meaningful insights to inform product development decisions.
